subject: math

objective.text: Solve two-step subtraction word problems with tape diagrams. Check answers by rounding.

explanations.title: Two-step problems
explanations.text: Find what is missing first, or find the total of the parts you know. Then use that to find the answer.

explanations.title: Estimate, then solve
explanations.text: Round the numbers first to get a general sense of the answer. Then find the exact answer and compare.

explanations.title: Reasonable answers
explanations.text: An answer is reasonable if it is near the estimate. Rounding the exact answer to the same place should match the estimate.

explanations.title: Compare with a smaller unknown
explanations.text: If one amount is fewer than another, subtract to find it. Then use both amounts to find the total.

explanations.title: Meters to centimeters
explanations.text: 1 meter is 100 centimeters. 1 m 20 cm is 100 plus 20, which is 120 centimeters.

questions.text: A farmer sold 25,196 pounds of potatoes on Monday and 18,023 on Tuesday. Round each to the nearest thousand and add. What is the estimate?
He sold 62,409 pounds in all. Round it to the nearest thousand and subtract 43,000. About how many pounds did he sell on Wednesday?
He sold 62,409 pounds in all, 25,196 on Monday and 18,023 on Tuesday. How many pounds did he sell on Wednesday?
The estimate is 19,000 and the exact answer is 19,190. Is the answer reasonable?
Pump A dispensed 241,752 gallons. Pump B dispensed 113,916 more gallons than Pump A. How many gallons did Pump B dispense?
Round 241,752 and 355,668 to the nearest hundred thousand and add. What is the estimate of the gallons both pumps dispensed?
Pump A dispensed 241,752 gallons and Pump B dispensed 355,668 gallons. How many gallons did both dispense?
The estimate is 600,000 and the exact answer is 597,420. Is the answer reasonable?
Martin's car had 86,456 miles. His wife drove 24,901 and his son drove 7,997. Round each to the nearest thousand. About how many miles did Martin drive?
Martin's car had 86,456 miles. His wife drove 24,901 and his son drove 7,997. How many miles did Martin drive?
The estimate is 53,000 and the exact answer is 53,558. Is the answer reasonable?
A class read 3,452 pages in week 1. In week 2 they read 4,090 more pages than in week 1. How many pages did they read in week 2?
The class read 3,452 pages in week 1 and 7,542 in week 2. How many pages did they read in all?
Round 3,452 and 7,542 to the nearest thousand and add. What is the estimate of the pages read?
A cargo plane weighed 500,000 pounds. After the first load came off it weighed 437,981 pounds. How many pounds were in the first load?
The first load was 62,019 pounds. Then 16,478 more pounds were taken off. How many pounds of cargo were removed in all?
Brett Favre passed for 71,838 yards. His best year was 4,413 yards and his second best year was 4,212. Round each to the nearest thousand. About how many yards were left?
Brett Favre passed for 71,838 yards. His best year was 4,413 yards and his second best year was 4,212. How many yards did he throw in the other years?
The estimate is 64,000 and the exact answer is 63,213. Is the answer reasonable?
Zachary's project had 95,234 words. He wrote 35,295 in month 1 and 19,240 in month 2. Round each to the nearest ten thousand. About how many words are left to write?
Zachary's project had 95,234 words. He wrote 35,295 in month 1 and 19,240 in month 2. How many words did he write in the rest of the semester?
The estimate is 40,000 and the exact answer is 40,699. Is the answer reasonable?
351,875 people downloaded an app in the first quarter. In the second quarter 101,949 fewer people downloaded it. How many downloaded it in the second quarter?
Round 351,875 and 249,926 to the nearest hundred thousand and add. What is the estimate of the downloads in two quarters?
351,875 people downloaded the app in the first quarter and 249,926 in the second. How many downloads were there in the two quarters?
The estimate is 600,000 and the exact answer is 601,801. Is the answer reasonable?
A store began a sale with 36,390 notebooks. It sold 7,424 in week 1 and 8,967 in week 2. How many notebooks were left?
Round 36,390, 7,424 and 8,967 to the nearest thousand to estimate the notebooks left. What is the estimate?
The estimate is 20,000 and the exact answer is 19,999. Is the answer reasonable?

hints.text: Think how many centimeters make 1 meter. Then add the extra centimeters.
Compare the largest unit first. Then compare the next place.
Find the whole and the part you know. Subtract to find the other part.
Round each number to the named place. Then add or subtract.
Do one step at a time. Use the first answer for the second step.
Round the exact answer to the same place as the estimate. Do they match?

assets_required.why_this_method: The lesson uses tape diagrams drawn on paper. The child cannot draw them.
assets_required.description: A tape diagram and vertical subtraction with an estimate box. The child rounds, estimates, finds the exact answer and compares.
must_show_exactly: A tape diagram with the whole, known parts and a variable
A vertical subtraction or addition with places lined up
An estimate box with a choice of place to round to
A compare row that shows the estimate next to the exact answer
A reasonable or not reasonable choice
assets_required.interaction: Child enters an estimate, works the exact answer, and the widget shows whether the two are close.
assets_required.alt_text: A tape diagram with an estimate and exact answer side by side.
assets_required.generation_caption: A clean tape diagram with a bracket and variable, a vertical computation beside it and an estimate box. [Build by code]
assets_required.review_notes: Source tape diagrams are drawn by the child. Build from the printed numbers.
